items.guidance: For each of the 19 s6-overlay services, check whether it is a oneshot or a longrun service; the named ones (init-complete, init-custom-init, init-env-file, init-folders) look like one-time setup steps, not long-running programs. Only longrun services need a worker declaration; fold no init step into a worker. If one service is a PostgreSQL or Redis server, report it as provided by Deployz.

List what the app writes under /usr/src/paperless/data and separate caches or indexes that can be rebuilt from documents that must survive a redeploy. If the app has a storage backend setting that accepts S3, report that setting and the bucket variable it reads so it can be mapped to STORAGE_BUCKET. Keep the local data directory as the default for other installs.

Run python src/manage.py migrate --noinput in a container built from this image with DATABASE_URL pointing at a disposable PostgreSQL, and confirm it exits 0 without prompts. Also check whether one of the s6-overlay init services already runs migrate at start; if so, report that service as the file that applies migrations.

Check which s6-overlay services start Celery (a worker, a beat scheduler, or both) and report each exact command and the Celery app module it loads. Report whether the Celery broker setting reads REDIS_URL or another variable name.
